Results.ReviewText: Still getting 'used' to how the grill heats and cooks. I really like the burner ignition sequence. The angled cross-section of the grates imparts a nice sear pattern to steaks and chicken. Makes it easier to clean than the round rungs on previous grills. The cooking surface size is just an inch shorter in length and width than the previous 4-burner grill this replaces. Only time will tell, but I like the cast aluminum design of the burner body. The burners and heat diffusers sit on cast shelves in the burner body, not sheet metal flanges. Those flanges all burned off in a year of use in the older grill.

Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I really like the quality of this grill.  It seems very well made and assembly was relatively straightforward.  I like the full cast iron bottom.  This grill does not skimp and use a stainless steal tray for the bottom, which rusts through so easily and is the reason we parted with our last grill.  It is a simple no frills grill that does what it is supposed to do.  My only knock is the burners so far seem a bit under powered.  The grill struggled to get up over 425 degrees in low 30 degree weather.  It will be fine in the warmer months but if you regularly grill year round and you want higher temps, you may want to look for more powerful burners.
Results.Title: Well made grill but a little underpowered.

45010001.Description:
Get ready to step up your grilling experience. As the family sits down for dinner, or a couple of friends come over for a bite – this three burner grill will do its magic. With the spacious cooking area you can sear steaks on one side while grilling an appetizer on the other, and the convenient open-cart allows you to keep your tools and equipment within reach. Armed with the strong GS4 grilling system, this gas grill is sure to take you and your meals to the next level.


 This product requires assembly.
